title: WORK-LAB local-model project permission matrix — which project may call which logical provider
purpose: Expresses brief section 10: a physical model is registered once by WORK-LAB and exposed to projects as a logical provider. ArcheAxis gets the full local AI base; WORK-LAB and DESIGN-LAB share only the common capabilities they actually need.
principle: Physical Model -> Runtime -> Provider -> Capability -> Project Permission

ArcheAxis-Knowledge-OS.role: The only project with a complete local AI base requirement.
ArcheAxis-Knowledge-OS.usage_contract: Consumes versioned Capability/Provider contracts only; never a file path, GGUF name or runtime executable.

WORK-LAB.role: Model control plane: discovery, registry, capability profile, provider config, local endpoints, runtime lifecycle, health, GPU/RAM state, context config, concurrency, task routing, benchmark, usage, latency, failure/restart/fallback, model version + file hash, license metadata, three-project sharing.
does_not_own: model weight copies outside the shared library

DESIGN-LAB.role: Design domain. Does NOT build a local model base.
allowed: call already-registered common providers on demand
forbidden: duplicating a model weight because it needs a capability
DESIGN-LAB.notes: ComfyUI/ visual weights already live in the shared library and are DESIGN-LAB-owned read-only territory for WORK-LAB; text/vision needs route through local.fast.default / local.deep.default.

permissions.note: DESIGN-LAB visual work uses its own ComfyUI chain, not this OCR provider

antiPatterns: A project starting its own llama.cpp/Ollama instance for the same model
A project storing a second copy of a weight file
A project hard-coding a GGUF name, quantization, or absolute path
Exposing the whole ArcheAxis ingestion pipeline to every project by default
Adding a second active provider for a capability without a golden-test failure
escalation: A project needing an archeaxis-first provider declares a concrete task; WORK-LAB flips that provider to ALLOW for that project and records the reason here.
